query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The integration of ultrasonic field-assisted metal additive manufacturing (U-FAAM) with traditional metal AM techniques can improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with potential defects and uneven microstructure
generation.conditions: Layer-by-layer deposition, various metal materials (aluminum alloys, magnesium alloys, titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys, steel), and controlled ultrasonic parameters (frequency, amplitude, duration)
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain structure, minimized porosity, and enhanced density
generation.mechanism: Acoustic cavitation and streaming disrupt dendrite formation, refine grain structure, and minimize porosity, thereby enhancing the density and mechanical properties of the metal components
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and reduced fabrication-induced defects
generation.baseline: Traditional metal additive manufacturing techniques without ultrasonic field assistance
generation.boundary: Limited by the feasibility of ultrasonic device design for high-temperature operations and the decrease in ultrasonic intensity with build height
generation.uncertainty: The optimal ultrasonic parameters and the effects of U-FAAM on different high-entropy alloys are still uncertain and require further research

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components using traditional metal AM techniques and U-FAAM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the U-FAAM technique does not show significant improvement in dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect density compared to traditional metal AM techniques, the hypothesis is falsified

## Abstract
AbstractMetal additive manufacturing (AM) is a disruptive technology that provides unprecedented design freedom and manufacturing flexibility for the forming of complex components. Despite its unparalleled advantages over traditional manufacturing methods, the existence of fatal issues still seriously hinders its large-scale industrial application. Against this backdrop, U-FAAM is emerging as a focus, integrating ultrasonic energy into conventional metal AM processes to harness distinctive advantages. This work offers an up-to-date, specialized review of U-FAAM, articulating the integrated modes, mechanisms, pivotal research achievements, and future development trends in a systematic manner. By synthesizing existing research, it highlights future directions in further optimizing process parameters, expanding material applicability, etc., to advance the industrial application and development of U-FAAM technology.Keywords: Metal additive manufacturing, Ultrasonic field-assisted manufacturing, 3D printing, U-FAAM mechanisms, Melt pool behavior, Research directions

The ultrasonic field profoundly affects the flow dynamics, temperature distribution and solidification mode of the microstructure in the melt pool , . The introduction of ultrasonic fields in AM brings numerous significant benefits to the printed materials, including: (1) reduced defects , ; (2) optimized microstructure ; (3) lowered thermal stress ; (4) improved interfacial bonding ; (5) increased material utilization ; (6) diversified material processing . Together, these advantages collectively propel the application of U-FAAM technology in the field of metal manufacturing and have established its key position in modern industry.
The motivation of this work is to provide a comprehensive and in-depth review of the latest research developments and application prospects of U-FAAM. In the field of U-FAAM, substrate UV amplitude modulation and moving UV amplitude modulation are regarded as two fundamental technological approaches. Fig. 1 demonstrates the widespread application of substrate UV amplitude modulation in conventional metal AM processes, encompassing WAAM , LDED  and LPBF . Slightly differently, the LDED process can further subdivision of the construction depending on whether the UV direction is parallel or perpendicular to the scan direction , . The utilization of moving UV amplitude modulation has only been documented in the WAAM and LDED processes . Given its propensity to disrupt the powder bed and induce powder scattering, moving UV amplitude modulation is not a viable option for the LPBF process.

This results in an increase in the density and mechanical properties of the metal parts. Furthermore, the technology facilitates rapid heat dissipation, narrowing the width of the heat-affected zone and minimizing thermal stress and deformation . In comparison to traditional substrate UV systems, this technology offers greater flexibility and maintains a constant ultrasonic intensity when manufacturing complex or large-scale components , .
Nevertheless, the implementation of moving UV amplitude modulation is not without its challenges.
